title: Veterinary Applications | BHOC Veterinary
description: Veterinary research contexts for Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier science, including companion-animal care, emergency oxygen support and wildlife medicine.
heading: Oxygen delivery. Species-specific evidence.
lead: BHOC is a development direction in precision oxygen therapeutics for settings where anemia or blood loss limits oxygen-carrying capacity.

areas.title: Companion-animal care
areas.text: Research questions around severe anemia, blood loss and practical oxygen-delivery support in dogs, cats and other companion animals.

areas.title: Emergency oxygen support
areas.text: Time-sensitive veterinary settings where donor blood may be delayed, unavailable or operationally difficult to provide.

areas.title: Wildlife medicine
areas.text: Species-specific research challenges in conservation medicine, zoological care and remote field environments.

regulatory.title: Oxyglobin and canine anemia.
paragraphs: In 1998, the FDA approved Oxyglobin, hemoglobin glutamer-200 (bovine), for anemia in dogs. This is a product-specific veterinary HBOC precedent.
The historical approval does not establish BHOC approval or suitability in other species. Each application requires its own evidence for dosing, safety and efficacy.
